productPageReviews.reviewTitle: After one month of usage - Worth for buyingAfter one month of usage - Worth for buying
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: One Month Review: OnePlus 13 (12GB+256GB, Midnight Blue Vegan Leather)​Purchase & Delivery ExperienceI ordered my OnePlus 13 during the Amazon Prime Day sale on July 2nd. By combining card offers, I managed to get it for a ₹50,000 budget. I had to purchase a Prime membership to avail the offer, which came with the promise of 2-day delivery. However, reading bad seller feedback and experiencing shipping delays made me lose trust in Amazon and their Open Box delivery system. I was genuinely worried if I would even receive the phone and prepared myself to inspect it meticulously.​By God's grace, the product was safely delivered on the 7th day! While the 2-day delivery promise for Prime members was broken, the Open Box delivery person was extremely polite, and my phone arrived in perfect condition.​Design: 4.9/5​I am reviewing this after a month of usage, starting with the design. I absolutely love the Midnight Blue color and the vegan leather back. It offers a premium in-hand feel and remains comfortable to hold for long periods. The physical alert slider is incredibly useful for silencing the phone in various situations without needing to wake the screen.​Processor: 5/5​The Snapdragon 8 Elite deserves a perfect rating. It is buttery smooth across the board—whether for regular, moderate, or heavy usage. Switching between background apps is seamless. For gaming, BGMI runs flawlessly on the highest graphics settings with an average frame rate of 118 FPS. The gameplay is incredibly smooth, and the phone only gets slightly warm during continuous gaming.​Display: 4.8/5​The 2K LTPO panel provides an immersive experience and flawlessly supports 4K HDR 60FPS videos on YouTube. I am giving it a 4.8 only because I upgraded from a Redmi Note 13 Pro Plus, which already had a great screen, so the jump wasn't mind-blowing for me. However, if you are upgrading from a standard display, this will easily be the greatest screen you've ever used.​Multimedia Experience: 4.9/5​Instead of Dolby Atmos, OnePlus included a Holo Audio system, and honestly, it performs even better. The stereo speakers provide a 360° surround sound experience that is loud, crisp, and has punchy bass.​Camera: 5/5​I am extremely satisfied and happy with this camera setup. The 50MP telephoto lens gives DSLRs a tough fight, and the edge detection on telephoto shots is perfect. It supports 8K video output, and you can remarkably shoot 4K 60FPS on both the front selfie and wide-angle cameras. Selfies come out crisp and full of detail. It packs all the premium features you could want, including cinematic mode and portrait video with a great bokeh effect. At the ₹50k price point, this camera setup is unmatched and competes directly with the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra and Vivo X300 variants.​Battery: 4.5/5​Even with over 50 apps installed, I get a solid average Screen-On Time (SOT) of 6.5 hours, which pushes to 7-8 hours under moderate use in some scenarios. The 100W fast charging is brilliant, taking just 38 to 42 minutes for a full charge under normal mode.​Overall Rating: 4.9/5​Note on OS Updates:I am intentionally keeping my phone on the out-of-the-box Android 15 software. I have seen a lot of videos indicating that the Android 16/July update severely reduces battery life to a maximum of 5 hours SOT. I am actively avoiding new updates until the community confirms that a patch has restored good battery life and SOT.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Absolute Performance Beast! Just Needs Camera Consistency to Be a True Flagship Killer
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Quick TakePros: Monstrous gaming performance, buttery-smooth OxygenOS, incredible battery life (on current updates), high peak photo quality.Cons: Camera white balance can be hit-or-miss; required a software patch to stabilize battery drain.Detailed Review1. Software & Hardware Performance — 10/10The hardware power OnePlus squeezed into this price tag is unbelievable. OxygenOS is silky smooth with zero stutters or UI lags anywhere.The real test, however, is heavy performance: running PC emulators. The chipset handles heavy titles like GTA V with surprising ease, maintaining stable frame rates without overheating. If raw processing speed and gaming performance are your main priorities, this phone is as fast as it gets.2. Battery Life & OS Updates — 8.5/10A word of advice for new buyers: Update your phone immediately.Out of the box on older builds, battery drain was quite inconsistent. However, after updating to the latest build of OxygenOS 16, the battery optimization improved dramatically. It now easily lasts a full day of heavy usage, rendering battery anxiety a thing of the past.3. Camera Performance — 7.5/10The camera system is a classic "hit or miss."When it hits: Photos come out stunning, offering flagship-level sharpness, detail, and dynamic range.When it misses: The software struggles with color temperature—the white balance can be all over the place, making photos look overly cool or warm depending on the scene's lighting.VerdictIf OnePlus focuses on tuning the camera algorithms for better white balance and color consistency via software patches, this device will be an undisputed flagship killer. Even with the minor camera quirks, for power users and gamers wanting top-tier performance at a fair price, it remains an easy recommendation

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Fantastic in every way barring Camera
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Coming from an iPhone 13, I found iOS to be extremely stable, with the most reliable camera I have ever used. However, it felt boring, restrictive, and backing up photos was honestly a painful process. These reasons led me to switch to Android. After careful consideration, I narrowed my choices down to the OnePlus 13 and the Samsung S24 Ultra. While the S24 Ultra is a bit pricey, the reports of the green line issue concerned me. Ultimately, OnePlus offering a lifetime screen replacement for green line issues sealed the deal for me.My Experience with the OnePlus 13Display, Haptics, Performance and Fingerprint Sensor: Excellent. No complaints. Feels premium.Battery: Phenomenal. I’m getting around 7 to 9 hours of screen-on time.Charging: The 100W SuperVOOC fast charging powers the 6000mAh battery in just 45 minutes—again, phenomenal.Refresh Rate, Sound, and Feel: All top-notch. It truly feels like a proper flagship.UI: It's clean. I like it.Camera: This is where the device falls short. With the iPhone 13, I never had to worry about picture quality—just point and shoot, and it always delivered excellent results. However, the OnePlus 13 is a bit inconsistent. In good lighting, it performs well, but in low light, it struggles, sometimes producing weird, blurry, ghostly images. I hope this is just a software issue that OnePlus can address with future updates. Unless they improve the camera significantly, it will never truly compete as a flagship. I personally feel OnePlus should ditch the Hasselblad branding and adopt Oppo's camera setup instead.Overall Impression:Coming back to OnePlus 13. While I'm not a gamer, I do take a lot of pictures, and this aspect leaves me wanting more. For someone who doesn't use the camera frequently, the OnePlus 13 will be a fantastic device and will take whatever beating you throw at it. Overall, I’d rate it a solid 4/5 and hope the Camera dept. gets huge budget next year.Edit. (after 3 months of usage).* Fingerprint reader with screen protector is a hit or miss. Being touted as the best, it really disappoints.* Video is very bad. It couldn't lock on to a single subject. Everytime I try to shoot with multiple people, it keeps saying use photo to lock onto single subject. Wth.!* Using the phone without case is a nightmare because of this all side curved edges. You can't hold the phone without touching the bottom edge of the phone. Since we are touching, it won't allow another touch. It's irritating and I had to slap a case on it.* Other things held up great. Battery, Performance, Haptics, OS. All great. (AI is useless. I guess it's useless everywhere). It's still a great phone if you are power user. If you want good quality photos and videos, look elsewhere.3.5 stars / 5.
